STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm; this one looks medium, about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the plate is about 1.1 pizza slices wide along its diagonal... using the pizza slice (about 11 cm long) as reference, the plate's side spans roughly 2.3 slice lengths, giving about 25 cm.
Final width: 25 cm (area 625 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pizza: 2 slices visible, both roughly 10 x 7 cm, no hidden pieces. Each slice is a standard piece of about 30 g of bread base plus cheese and tomato sauce. Slice weight per piece is roughly 60-70 g, so 2 slices ≈ 130 g. Using the slice rule (bread slice 30 g, plus topping), I estimate about 2 x 65 = 130 g.
- Lettuce/leafy greens (dressed, looks like cooked-ish creamy Caesar-style leaves): footprint roughly 20% of plate area ≈ 125 cm2. Loose leaves 3-6 cm, but these are compressed, so average thickness about 1.5 cm (flat layer effect). Volume ≈ 125 x 1.5 = 188 ml. Raw-ish leafy greens with dressing: bulk density about 0.3 g/ml. Grams ≈ 56 g. Dressing adds sauce, so take ~60 g total for greens including dressing.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible beneath the pizza or greens; the plate centre is bare.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Pizza (cheese and tomato, cooked): about 260 kcal/100 g.
- Dressed lettuce (Caesar-style with creamy dressing): about 150 kcal/100 g.

Totals: pizza 130 g, greens 60 g, total about 190 g.
Energy: pizza 130 x 2.6 = 338 kcal; greens 60 x 1.5 = 90 kcal; total ≈ 430 kcal.
